```yaml
name: AMPCode PR Review

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - staging
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: ampcode-pr-review-${{ github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '16'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install -g @sourcegraph/amp

      - name: Run AMPCode analysis
        id: ampcode-analysis
        run: |
          amp analyze --max-files 50 --file-types ts,tsx,js,jsx,py
          echo "::set-output name=comments::$(cat results.json | jq -r '.comments')"
        env:
          AMPCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AMPCODE_API_KEY }}

      - name: Post review comments
        if: success()
        run: |
          echo "${{ steps.ampcode-analysis.outputs.comments }}" | jq -c .[] | xargs -I {} curl -X POST \
            -H "Authorization: token ${{ github.token }}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{}' \
            https://api.github.com/repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/reviews
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
```

This GitHub Actions workflow file sets up a job named `review` that triggers on pull request events for the `main` and `staging` branches. It checks out the code, sets up Node.js, installs the Ampcode CLI, runs the Ampcode analysis on up to 50 changed files of specific types, and posts structured review comments directly on the PR using the GitHub API. The workflow includes concurrency control to handle multiple PRs efficiently.
